conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: TERMINATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format `TERMINATE { report-name-1 } ...` (cite.py --check 14.9.46.2 "TERMINATE" -> OK §14.9.46.2 General format). Grammar `terminateStatement : TERMINATE reportName+ ;` admits one-or-more report-names, ungated (Core grammar); BindTerminate resolves each name (SR1 COBOLNET1757 on an unknown one). Probed: single-report TERMINATE compiles and runs at --std 85, 2002, 2023 (out/probe/terminate-statement/q85.cob, q2002.cob, p1.cob); three-name `TERMINATE R-C R-B R-A` compiles and runs at 2023 (p2.cob). No spec-derived test targets the general format itself; Terminate_Gr2/ControlBreak tests exercise only the one-name form. [editions as adjudicated: 1985 (Report Writer module), 2002, 2014, 2023]

rows.subject: TERMINATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.46.3 "shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement" -> OK §14.9.46.3 3). CheckCrossStatementBans scans region B (imperative-statement-1 plus every WHEN/FINALLY body — the whole PERFORM) for terminateStatement with reportName().Length > 1 -> COBOLNET1606. The ban counts report-name OCCURRENCES, matching the rule's 'specifies more than one report-name'. Probed out/probe/terminate-statement: s1.cob (TERMINATE R-A R-B in imperative-statement-1, WHEN EC-ALL) -> COBOLNET1606; s2.cob (in the WHEN body) -> COBOLNET1606; s3.cob (two single-name TERMINATEs in imperative-statement-1) compiles and runs (OK). At --std 2014 the PERFORM itself is refused by COBOLNET0900 (s4.cob). No negative golden for COBOLNET1606 exists (grep tests/conformance/negative). [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (the exception-checking PERFORM is new in 2023 — VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 79, Annex E.3.3 item 36)]
rows.rule-text: A TERMINATE statement that specifies more than one report-name shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.

rows.subject: TERMINATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.46.4 "processing resumes at the next implicit TERMINATE statement" -> OK §14.9.46.4 4). BindTerminate builds one BoundTerminate per report-name in written order inside a BoundImplicitSeries (the PB419 per-implicit-statement boundary mechanism; ImplicitStatementSeriesDriftTests enumerates TERMINATE). Both sentences probed: out/probe/terminate-statement/p2.cob, TERMINATE R-C R-B R-A with R-A and R-C active and R-B never initiated, >>TURN EC-REPORT-INACTIVE CHECKING ON and a USE AFTER EC-REPORT-INACTIVE declarative doing RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT: output HANDLED-I, AFTER; R-C's file carries RFC and R-A's carries RFA — R-C terminated first, the R-B implicit TERMINATE raised, processing resumed at the NEXT implicit TERMINATE (R-A), not after the whole statement. No spec-derived golden pins either sentence for TERMINATE. [editions as adjudicated: sentence 1: 1985 (Report Writer module), 2002, 2014, 2023; sentence 2 (RESUME NEXT STATEMENT): 2002, 2014, 2023]
rows.rule-text: The result of executing a TERMINATE statement in which more than one report-name-1 is specified is as though a separate TERMINATE statement had been executed for each report-name-1 in the same order as specified in the statement. If an implicit TERMINATE statement results in the execution of a declarative procedure that executes a RESUME statement with the NEXT STATEMENT phrase, processing resumes at the next implicit TERMINATE statement, if any.

rows.subject: TERMINATE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.46.4 "does not close the file associated with report-name-1" -> OK §14.9.46.4 6). TerminateCore touches no connector state (only `_active`/`_started`); the file is closed by the program's own CLOSE. Probed out/probe/terminate-statement/p1.cob: after TERMINATE (twice) a CLOSE of the report file returns FILE STATUS 00 (a closed file would give 42), and a second INITIATE on the same still-open file succeeds; p3.cob likewise CLOSE FS=00. Terminate_Gr2 CLOSEs after TERMINATE but asserts no status, so it does not pin this rule. [editions as adjudicated: 1985 (Report Writer module), 2002, 2014, 2023]
rows.rule-text: The TERMINATE statement does not close the file associated with report-name-1.

rows.subject: TURN directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 "the effect is as if file-name-1 were specified for each of these exception-names" OK. Level-2 half: DirectiveCovers -> TryGet(level-2) && UnderLevel2(level3); WARNING excluded. File-name half: the Fold keeps the (EC-I-O, F1) event and matches it only for a query naming F1. Probes: TRNF1 '>>TURN EC-I-O F1 CHECKING ON' -> READ F2 AT END: status spaces, READ F1 AT END: EC-I-O-AT-END (expected per GR3 second sentence); TRNO2 '>>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON' does not enable EC-I-O-WARNING (status 05 -> spaces). Both halves verified. Test-ref left empty: conformance-test:ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.Turn_Level2_CoversItsChildren and unit:TurnStateTests.Level2_EnablesItsChildrenOnly witness the first sentence only; no spec-derived test witnesses the level-2 + file-name-1 sentence (test-needed). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the TURN directive is a COBOL-2002 introduction; §7.3 compiler directives)
rows.rule-text: With the exception of EC-I-O-WARNING, if exception-name-1 is one of the level-2 exception-names, the effect is as if that TURN directive were specified containing all exception-names that are subordinate to that level-2 exception-name. If file-name-1 is specified, the effect is as if file-name-1 were specified for each of these exception-names.

rows.subject: TURN directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 "may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly within a TURN directive" OK. TURN half (probes via OPEN INPUT of a missing OPTIONAL file, status 05): TRNO1 EC-ALL ON -> not raised; TRNO2 EC-I-O ON -> not raised; TRNO3 EC-I-O-WARNING ON -> EC-I-O-WARNING; TRNO4 then EC-ALL OFF -> still raised; TRNO5 then EC-I-O OFF -> still raised; TRNO6 then EC-I-O-WARNING OFF -> not raised. PERFORM half: TRNQ1 'PERFORM OPEN INPUT F2 WHEN EC-I-O-WARNING ...' -> the WHEN runs with EC-I-O-WARNING; after END-PERFORM a second OPEN (status 05) does not raise it (status stays the EC-USER-X raised between); TRNQ2 WHEN EC-I-O and TRNQ3 WHEN EC-ALL do not enable it. All four halves verified. Test-ref empty: unit:TurnStateTests.EcAll_DoesNotEnableIoWarning witnesses only the TURN on/EC-ALL arm; the WHEN-phrase and end-of-PERFORM arms have no spec-derived witness. SIBLING DEFECT FOUND WHILE PROBING (not this rule's): a SUCCESSFUL READ with a nonzero status never calls the EC hook, so EC-I-O-WARNING is never raised by READ even when explicitly enabled — see findings (§9.1.13.1). || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (EC-I-O-WARNING and the exception-checking PERFORM are COBOL-2023 additions, Annex E)
rows.rule-text: The exception-name EC-I-O-WARNING may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly within a TURN directive or by its presence in a WHEN phrase in an exception-checking PERFORM statement. Similarly, it may be turned off only by an explicit TURN directive or the end of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.

rows.subject: TURN directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 "the TURN directive does not apply to any phrase of that statement" OK. Enablement is keyed on the statement's START line with strict eventLine < statementLine (directive lines are blanked, line-count preserving). Probe TRNG5: 'ADD 1 TO A' / '>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON' / 'ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY ... ADD 1 TO B ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY ...' -> P1 [spaces] (the ADD whose phrase follows the TURN is NOT checked) and P2 [EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION] (the nested ADD inside the phrase, a succeeding statement, IS checked). TRNG5B: OFF written inside an IF disables the nested ADD and the ADD after END-IF (both spaces). Both sentences verified. kb/Work PB963 (open) owns this row's witness debt — test-ref left empty; unit:TurnStateTests.Directive_AppliesToSucceedingStatementsOnly covers only the strict-line half. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the TURN directive is a COBOL-2002 introduction; §7.3 compiler directives)
rows.rule-text: If specified within a statement, the TURN directive does not apply to any phrase of that statement. That TURN directive applies to any succeeding statement in the sequence of source lines, whether or not that succeeding statement is within the scope of the statement in which the TURN directive is specified.
